record_type_quote: The purpose of this study was to replicate Rousmaniere et al. (2014) by examining the amount of variance in client treatment outcome as measured by the Outcome Questionnaire-45.2 (OQ-45.2) accounted for by supervisors and therapists and to provide an extended analysis of client treatment duration at the supervisor and therapist levels.

targets.authors: Rousmaniere, T. G., Swift, J. K., Babins-Wagner, R., Whipple, J. L., & Berzins, S.
targets.title: Supervisor effects on client outcome in routine practice.
targets.evidence_quote: The purpose of this study was to replicate Rousmaniere et al. (2014) by examining the amount of variance in client treatment outcome as measured by the Outcome Questionnaire-45.2 (OQ-45.2) accounted for by supervisors and therapists and to provide an extended analysis of client treatment duration at the supervisor and therapist levels.
targets.outcome_quote: Results from this replication suggest the effects found in Rousmaniere and colleagues (2014) were not site-specific. Rather, the lack of variance in client outcome accounted for by supervisors could be observed in a different counseling center with a similarly large data set.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The original near-zero supervisor variance is confirmed in a different counseling-center sample. Treatment duration was not examined in the original and is an extension; limitations about causal effects do not negate the successful comparison of supervisor variance.

reasoning: Different archival counseling-center sample re-tests Rousmaniere et al. The reference list prints its original title as Supervisor effects on client outcome in routine practice and dates it 2014; those are copied as printed. Other supervision studies are background comparisons rather than identified targets. Full 11-page publisher PDF text, authors and title verified.
